description: Proof that a parent or guardian consented to this child's profile, verified by a code sent to their own phone. This is the record India's DPDP Act 2023 asks for: it stores WHAT was agreed to (the exact bilingual text, snapshotted, not a pointer to text that can later be edited), WHEN, and HOW the number was proven — and it stores no phone number, only its HMAC and last 4 digits.

fields.description: Denormalised so the record reads without a join while it lives. It does NOT outlive the learner: delete_student erases this whole row, because keeping a child's name in order to prove we were permitted to keep her name is not a retention basis.
fields.label: Student name

fields.description: The challenge that proved the number. Kept as the audit chain; it holds no number and no code.
fields.label: Verified by challenge

fields.description: How the facilitator obtained this permission — met the guardian, phone call, signed paper form. Only meaningful when channel is Facilitator; a device-proven consent needs no explanation beyond the challenge it links to.
fields.label: How consent was given (facilitator)

fields.description: Snapshot of the exact wording shown at the time, in both languages. Snapshotted deliberately: consent to wording that has since been rewritten is not consent to the new wording.
fields.label: Consent text (as shown)

fields.description: Set when a guardian withdraws consent. DPDP gives them that right, and withdrawal must be as easy as giving it.
fields.label: Withdrawn on

name: Hikmat Consent
